Recommendation

Receive item on Silicon Valley Express Lanes (SVEL) Program with focused discussion related to the SVEL Strategic Plan.

 

Item Discussion

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

At its December 2008 meeting, the Board approved the Silicon Valley Express Lanes (SVEL) Program. VTA has developed the SVEL Strategic Plan covering Fiscal Years 2026 to 2035. The SVEL Strategic Plan outlines a phased project delivery approach highlighting near-term (Attachment A) (3 to 5 years), mid-term (5 to 10 years), and long-term (beyond 10 years) milestones. The SVEL Strategic Plan also presents several key policy areas of the SVEL Program and provides recommendations for future related action items.

 

·              The purpose of this item to be brought to the Board Workshop is to provide the Board of Directors with an opportunity to receive staff input on areas of focus on the SVEL Strategic Plan where feedback was received from the Committees and public.

·              The Board input will allow staff to refine the SVEL Strategic Plan before the report is finalized.   

 

STRATEGIC PLAN/GOALS:

The SVEL Program aligns with VTA’s Business Line 3: Transportation Systems Management, in providing support to its member agencies in transportation systems management, funding, integration, and innovation. The SVEL Program supports Business Line 1: Faster, Frequent, Reliable Transit, as it is proposed to provide funding for transit, and supports Business Line 2: Delivering Projects and Programs, as it is proposed to be a funding source for multimodal corridor improvements.

The SVEL Program tolling system assets are owned and operated by VTA with policy direction provided by the VTA Board in a manner consistent with core values in the VTA Strategic Plan. The most relevant core goals in the VTA Strategic Plan include delivering the SVEL Program by maximizing user benefits, strengthening compliance, protecting revenue integrity, and reinforcing public confidence. Another core goal is to accelerate the delivery of express lanes to generate revenue and to provide revenue diversification for the agency for long-term financial sustainability.

 

Body

BACKGROUND:

 

At its December 2008 meeting, the Board approved the SVEL Program to provide congestion relief by implementing a roadway pricing system that enables the use of unused capacity in carpool lanes. This is accomplished by allowing solo commuters to use the available capacity in the carpool lanes for a fee. The fee changes dynamically in response to congestion levels and the available capacity in the lanes. The result of these changes is the implementation of express lanes on what were formerly carpool lanes and, in some cases, the construction of additional lanes to support operations and safety.

The SVEL Program’s primary objectives include:

·              Provide congestion relief through more effective use of existing roadways.

·              Provide commuters with a new mobility option.

·              Establish a new funding source for transportation improvements including public transit.

The SVEL Program consists of two corridors, namely US 101/SR 85 and SR 237/I-880. The state law that authorized tolling on these two corridors stipulates that net revenues generated in each corridor be used within the same corridor for transportation improvement projects, including support for transit operations and carpool lanes. Caltrans owns the underlying roadway on which VTA has built the express lanes, while VTA owns the signs, sensors, and communication equipment that comprise the express lanes tolling system.

The SVEL Program has served over 46 million toll users to date, providing key operational benefits with average operating speeds exceeding 45 miles per hour and ensuring travel time reliability, resulting in travel time savings of up to 20 minutes. The SVEL Program has generated positive net revenues since its inception.

DISCUSSION:

 

The SVEL Strategic Plan aligns with the overall VTA Strategic Plan (currently under development) by meeting the agency's goals of improved mobility, financial sustainability, and economic development. This first iteration of the SVEL Strategic Plan documents the history and development, goals and objectives, and operational policies for the SVEL Program. The Board Workshop will provide an opportunity for the Board to engage with VTA staff to provide input and directions.

 

CLIMATE IMPACT:

 

Express lanes improves system efficiency by enhancing operations as a congestion relief management tool and by moving more people more efficiently within a shorter period. The SVEL Program promotes increased person throughput by providing toll free travel and toll discounts for eligible carpoolers and higher vehicle occupancy. The toll revenues from the SVEL Program are planned to be allocated to support transit operations, amongst other corridor improvements. Based on the above factors, the SVEL Program is estimated to not have a negative climate impact. It should be noted that the effects of each project on the climate, which has yet to be environmentally approved, would be evaluated during each project's environmental review process.
